consumer: The mission/dialogue condition lambda built by conditional_t::set_has_item, asking 'does this actor possess >=1 of item X (charges_of>0 or has_amount>=1)?' and returning that yes/no to the dialogue/eligibility evaluator.
scope: only the character's own carried items (wielded/worn/inventory and their non-gun/non-magazine container contents) — on-person possession, not nearby/reachable inventory
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_item — its body returns actor->charges_of(item_id) > 0 || actor->has_amount(item_id, 1), an engine-COMPUTED possession predicate over the character actor; this is the authority the mission/dialogue check consumes, not the carried_items serialization (write_carried_items) or the traversal step (visit_internal).
divergence: Avatar's only copy of item X is ammo loaded inside a magazine (or gun): visit_internal deliberately does NOT descend into gun/magazine contents, so the engine has_amount/charges_of predicate answers FALSE, while a re-derivation that naively scans nested container contents from the snapshot would answer TRUE — exposing the wrong authority.
